text:
Ryan Winterton has gone eleven straight games without a point, and our numbers say it is not all bad luck. The 23-year-old Kraken forward, a third-round pick in 2021, is playing about 13 minutes a night in a depth role, and over his last ten games his line has created a bit less (4.2 on-ice expected goals, the quality of chances, against 5.0 usual).

The finishing is the other half. He has two goals on 4.5 expected, shooting 6.9%, under the low end of our range for him. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking liked where he goes: 6.3 scoring chances per 60 from the home-plate area in front of the net last season, 81st percentile. Players who keep getting there tend to score eventually.

His five-on-five shot share is poor (38.4% of attempts), but chance quality is closer to even (48.1%) and better than Seattle manages without him. Evolving-Hockey noted he played with weak teammates last season. One thing to watch: he got 19:36 and four shots against Vancouver on Nov. 19, his most ice time in weeks.
headline: Ryan Winterton is waiting on a bounce
